item.title: Go Get In Some ‘Good Trouble’: All the Activist Groups Bruce Springsteen Has Backed on His Land of Hope and Dreams Tour
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our show, where music meets activism. Tonight, we're talking about Bruce Springsteen's latest tour, the Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour. Springsteen and the E Street Band have been traveling the country, performing in cities from coast to coast, but this tour is about more than just the music.
[Soft music transitions in]
Host: Each night, Springsteen has been using his platform to call upon the power of art and music to defend American ideals and values. He's partnered with over 20 activist organizations, working on the front lines of democracy and human rights, to bring awareness and support to their causes.
[Music transitions to a clip of Springsteen's concert]
Host: During his shows, Springsteen has been welcoming these organizations into the venues, giving them the opportunity to reach out to his fans and solicit support. And it's not just about raising awareness – Springsteen is encouraging his fans to take action.
[Clip of Springsteen's voice: "When you go home tonight, hold your loved ones close. And in the morning … find a way to take aggressive, peaceful action to defend our country's ideals"]
Host: At each show, Springsteen has been ending with a call to action, urging his fans to get involved and make a difference. He's even been partnering with specific organizations, like the American Civil Liberties Union, to support their work in defending human rights.
[Music transitions back to the host]
Host: So, what happens when the show is over? The music may stop, but the impact doesn't have to. Springsteen is showing us that music can be a powerful catalyst for change, inspiring us to take action and make a difference in our communities.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our show. Remember, as Springsteen says, "go on out and get into some 'good trouble'." [Outro music continues to play until the end]
